output.brief: FCR fell because of the 14 April Finance change, not the new starters. It cut agents' in-call credit limit from £100 to £25 and automatically refers larger adjustments to the Billing Resolution team. Billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54%, and referred calls resolve at about 33% against 82% for the others. Referral rates and the FCR drop are nearly identical across new and tenured agents, so inexperience is not the driver. Tariff mix barely changed FCR within each contact reason. The sharp fall began the week of the Finance change, though the IVR change (28 April) was not separately tested. I'm fairly confident. Don't put the April intake on performance plans; that would punish the wrong group. Next: agree a revised in-call credit limit with Finance and trial it on two teams for six weeks, with post-call sampling of credits. Track FCR and the unsupported-credit rate, which Finance wants below 1% of value. MI can produce the team-level breakdown within a day. Don't pause the IVR work on this evidence. Don't spend three months rebuilding the dashboard yet.
